chapter: Army, return to El Paso and Mardi Gras parades
title: The Lions Club parade day: hours, pay and the St. Charles reviewing stand
summary: Watts recounts the all-day march with one hour's break for 35 cents, from Luzon and Ferret to Canal Street.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Well, now we got 35 cents, man, for all day. Yeah. I mean, you trucked. The only break we got was at Padra Street. Mm-hmm. You know where they got that place that they eat and all? Yeah, I do. Yeah. That was, they let us stop there about an hour.
And that's all from 7.30 to 4.30, because I kept the time right on them.
Well, it was before 7.30, just a little, huh? Oh, yeah.
When we started out? Mm-hmm. Oh, yeah. Yeah. Before 7.30. Oh, yeah.
I got that before 7.30 and I...

See, because I met them at Luzon and Ferret at 6.30. Mm-hmm. And Anderson wasn't long picking us up. And we hit right on out there to where they were farming at. See, what street was that? Who was it player for? Carson Noble, way out there in the Irish Channel. Who was it player for? Lions.
But it was up there, right by Alderman Park, Henry Clay, I think, when I called you.
Oh, that's where they left from, way up there. Yeah. Well, they didn't leave from the Lions Club. Mm-mm. The Lions is the Lion and Nance Asian.
Yeah, yeah. That's where we broke up at. That's where you broke up. Yeah. But no, they was further up in that gate.
Oh, yeah. About Alderman Park. Well, yeah, man. That's where they leave from. Buzzards and all that gate.

I never saw so much of St. Charles Avenue. Looked like I walked around the Belt before we hit Canal Street. Jesus, God. And when you get down to St. Charles, just like I told you before, both them bands is working. Mm-hmm. And I understood Anderson and Broussard. What? Say, now when we get there in front of all them people, the reviewing stand is just packed. Rex is reviewing stands all of them. Say, keep both them bands going. And we did that all the way down to St. Charles Canal and then turned Canal and kept both the bands going. He's playing different numbers. Soon they get down one number they pick up another one. And Tony went to the magazine and started back up. Lordy, I'm with you.
